mechanics.premise: The text reasons toward an impartial concern that includes even those who harm the one who holds it (dossier section D).
tone_mechanisms_observed: equalizing of self and other: the rhetorical ground on which impartial compassion is argued (dossier section E)
exchanging of self and other: the practitioner's concern relocated from self-preference to the other's freedom from suffering (dossier section E)
impartial scope with no conditionality: concern universal in scope and obligation-bearing, distinguished from pity and sentimental attachment (dossier sections A, E)
mechanics.style_and_devices: Equalizing and exchanging of self and other as the machinery of the argument; impartial, unconditional scope rather than preferential care (dossier sections D, E).
mechanics.scope_note: Sanskrit original (dossier section F); the dossier records karuna among the Sanskrit/Pali/Chinese terms that are not exact equivalents of the English 'compassion', so the work is cited for structure and stance, not as a lexical equivalent (dossier sections E, I); region follows section E's Indian framing; no page, DOI, or quotation was added.
mechanics.verification_note: Sanskrit; Wallace & Wallace trans. Snow Lion 1997 confirmed; described, not quoted (dossier section F).
